content: List my rides from the last two weeks, then pull the full details of the hardest one and tell me what stands out.

Here's the picture across your last two weeks:

| Date | Name | Duration | Load | Intensity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jun 24 | Endurance spin | 1h 30m | 55 | 0.70 |
| Jun 28 | Hill repeats | 1h 20m | 88 | 0.70 |
| Jul 2 | Long ride | 3h 00m | 120 | 0.70 |

---

**Deep look: Long Ride — July 2nd**

The headline number that stands out is **load 120 over exactly 3 hours** — that's a meaningful chunk of aerobic work, the kind of session that takes 48–72 hours to absorb properly. It's your heaviest hit in the two-week window by a clear margin (roughly 37% more than the Hill repeats).

One thing catches my eye though: **all three rides show the same intensity factor of 0.70**. That's solidly Z2/endurance territory, which is fine for a long ride — but it also means the Hill repeats at intensity 0.70 look identical to the long ride on that metric. That suggests either the hill efforts weren't quite pushing into threshold/VO2max territory, or the intensity figure is averaged out and the peaks aren't fully surfaced here. Worth keeping in mind when judging how much top-end stress you've actually accumulated.

The detail returned from intervals.icu for this ride is minimal — no per-lap splits, no HR drift, no power curve — so I can't tell you how you faded across the 3 hours or whether your heart rate decoupled. If you have a head unit file for this ride and it's been uploaded fully, a `/review deep` on it would give you pacing quartiles, decoupling, and best-effort peaks.

**What this means for the next session:** After a load-120 long ride four days ago, you're likely still carrying some fatigue. If today or tomorrow is your next session, lean toward Z2 or a light sweet-spot block — nothing that stacks more threshold stress on top until you see how the legs feel.
